feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 9 (the same geometry, controller and gains as this package) raced with zero line-loss events on the oval, S-bend and slalom, against 0.05 to 1.0 events in iterations 5 to 8. Oval finished 8 of 20 seeds, with steering_oscillation 0.228. Max_error stayed at 0.0552 m on the oval, 0.0601 m on the S-bend and 0.0624 m on the slalom, all just above or at the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 8 to 9 showed that raising kd from 0.30 to 0.35 cleared the residual bend losses. I have kept the controller unchanged, since the Integrator's rule is to change gains only when oscillation rises well above 0.23 on the oval, and it did not. The one geometry lever left is wheel_track. Per the contract's turn-rate formula, a narrower track gives more yaw per PWM difference, so 0.09 m is the physically motivated direction, though it has not been raced. The Integrator cannot test a change after this race, so the choice rests on the evidence above. If the final race keeps line loss at 0 and max_error at or above 0.06 m on the bends, the bend authority is the limit. If line loss returns, the controller was tuned to the 0.10 m track, and the narrower track raises effective gain by about 11 percent, so the change would be risky.
requested_changes: Set wheel_track to 0.09 m only if the team is willing to accept an untested change on the final race. Iteration 9 has max_error of 0.0601 m on the S-bend and 0.0624 m on the slalom, so yaw authority is the stated limit, and the contract formula says a narrower track adds yaw per PWM difference.

If wheel_track 0.09 m is used, keep kp 2.2 and kd 0.35 unchanged. Iteration 9 shows oscillation at 0.228 on the oval, and the 11 percent rise in effective gain could push it over the 0.23 trigger. Lower kp first, not geometry, if that happens.

Keep sensor_size 0.016 and the seven sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m and y = 0.04 m. Iterations 3 to 9 show this span clears oval line loss and keeps S-bend and slalom losses at zero in iteration 9, so no sensor change is supported.
